topics.definition: Docker volumes provide persistent storage for container data.
topics.example: Store database files in a volume
tips: Use volumes for data that must survive container removal.

topics.definition: Bind mounts connect a host directory directly to a container.
topics.example: Mount project folder into a container

topics.definition: Named volumes are managed by Docker and are easier to reuse.
topics.example: Attach myvolume to a database container
tips: Prefer named volumes for production data.

topics.definition: Volumes can be created, attached, detached and removed independently of containers.
topics.example: Reuse the same volume across containers

topics.definition: Volumes preserve data even after containers are deleted.
tips: Store important application data in volumes.

topics.definition: Volumes can be backed up and restored to protect important data.
Docker provides commands to list, inspect and remove volumes.
Use persistent volumes, back up data and clean up unused volumes regularly.
tips: Avoid storing important data inside containers.
